chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is the ruling regarding the two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer? When is their time?' He said: 'Before the rising of the dawn (sun). When the dawn rises, the time for the dawn prayer has entered.'
ai.seo_question: When should the two sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr prayer be performed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr are performed before the emergence of true dawn ( طلوع الفجر ), not merely before sunrise, thereby distinguishing the specific time of the sunnah from the obligatory prayer's onset. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for ensuring the sunnah is completed within its proper window before the adhan for Fajr is called. The hadith underscores the precision required in prayer timings, linking the physical act of worship to the celestial signs mentioned in the Quran.
